execution.result_contract: Source validation emits compact mode results; installation emits OK on payload-free success or one structured phase, skill, rollback, and reason blocker; inventory writes valid routing entries and malformed direct-manifest blockers to the caller-selected file and emits OK.

checks.pass_condition: The source manifest declares a nonempty stable runtime_source_id and either the ceratops or ceratops-compatible validation profile; full validation always applies common checks and only the ceratops profile adds Ceratops-specific icon, contract, retired-artifact, and repository-governance checks.

A skill-bearing source repository bootstrap declares one positive internal INSTALLER_VERSION. The bootstrap is standard-library-only, renders selected skills and overlays their files without content validation, retirement, or lifecycle runtime calls, retains destination-only files and other skills, exposes only repo-root, install-root, and skill inputs, preserves input parsing and path safety, and cleans only bootstrap-owned staging and locks. Copy failures may leave partial updates. Managed runtime CLI and manifests contain no installer-version field.

deterministic_evidence: source SKILL.md section and subsection structure
checks.pass_condition: Source skill frontmatter contains only name and description; name matches the directory, contains 1 to 64 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens, does not start or end with a hyphen, and contains no consecutive hyphens; description contains 40 to 1024 characters; the body contains a Markdown H2 section structure; the ceratops profile additionally requires Boundaries and Output Contract subsections.

OpenAI interface metadata exists, default_prompt names the skill, display name resembles the skill identity, and short description contains 25 to 64 characters and overlaps the trigger description; the ceratops profile additionally requires icon fields, shared Ceratops icon paths, and matching bytes.

deterministic_evidence: managed and standalone installation behavior tests
checks.pass_condition: Every source skill has a manifest assignment including core. Optional actions maps skill names to uniquely routed direct references/*.md action paths and nonempty section-ID lists; missing skills, unknown sections, unsafe paths, non-action targets, repeated sections, inherited skill sections, and generated markers in source actions are rejected. Skill-level assignments and canonical shared-section inputs are preserved. Each action's ordered shared content is inserted exactly once after its H1 only in installed copies, consistently across managed and independent installers. Source SKILL.md and action files remain delta-only. A repository with no source skills has empty skill, action, and canonical-section maps.

Every skill assigned the multi-action-skill section has one complete Action References index with at least two unique direct references/*.md paths; every mapped file exists and uses an Action title, and every top-level reference with an Action title is indexed.

Each skill folder contains `SKILL.md` and may contain `README.md` as its only top-level files and uses only profile-supported resource directories; the compatible profile may include `tests/`, while the ceratops profile allows `agents/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, and `references/`. Reference files remain at the reference root or in the supported contracts, schemas, and templates collections. Multi-skill executable sources remain under `skills/sections/scripts`, separate from repository-maintenance scripts.

deterministic_evidence: declared payload source and target paths
versioned shared skill Python environment behavior tests
checks.pass_condition: Runtime payload declarations use either an existing repo-relative path or matching glob copied at its source-relative target, or an exact `source` and installed-skill-relative `target` mapping. Exact mappings select one file, all paths are portable, installed targets are collision-free, single-skill executable sources are skill-owned, and multi-skill executable sources remain under `skills/sections/scripts`. Each source repository owns its Python project and lock under `skills/sections/python`; runtime payloads never copy either into an installed skill. Deployment prepares a versioned shared environment only for declared Python skills, records its interpreter only in their installed manifests, and never modifies an environment already used by a helper.

The installer resolves an explicit, base-revision, or all-managed affected set before mutation and invokes one locked batch transaction. Every selected present skill stages and validates before canonical mutation; existing targets retire, the complete staged batch activates, and pre-commit failures restore the prior batch. Targeted installs remove only declared absent skills; all-managed installs include same-source stale skills. For an authorized source-identity rename, an exact previous identity admits only current or previous ownership and the transaction persists only the current identity. Inventory reads direct manifests only and does not claim runtime validation.
Every source skill has a row in the README Skills table and every row in that table points to an existing source skill directory, without requiring a name prefix.
Files copied into or rendered into managed runtime skills do not contain high-confidence secret patterns or user-local absolute filesystem paths.

The source-doc registry and contract-review action own skill-design standards refresh. The source-validate action invokes the existing bundle-owned validator in full, selected-skill, or sections mode; deployment requires its passing full result for unchanged source inputs. The separate skills-consistency-review action owns manual non-deterministic compliance without silently changing the contracts.

deterministic_evidence: structured runtime manifests and section assignments
skill deterministic and nondeterministic contract mappings
checks.pass_condition: Full source validation checks structured repository data, portable runtime inputs, current skill identities, README alignment, and profile-aware governance. Executable behavior is established through import, CLI, filesystem-state, and transaction tests rather than source markers, syntax-tree form, source hashes, or executable source-anchor metadata.
